blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A budget is a plan for the money. Before the year starts, the team decides how much they will spend and how much they will earn, month by month.

A forecast is different. It is an updated guess during the year. It is based on what has really been happening. The budget gives discipline: "this is what we agreed to spend." The forecast gives reality: "this is where we are really going."

Good companies use both. Without a budget, teams spend with no limits. Without a forecast, they walk into surprises. Good financial management needs both.

items.q: What is a budget?
items.why: "A budget is a plan for the money."

items.q: When does the team decide how much to spend and earn?
items.why: "Before the year starts, the team decides how much they will spend and earn."

items.q: A forecast is based on…
items.why: "It is based on what has really been happening."

items.q: The text suggests that a team with no forecast will…
items.why: Inferência: "Without a forecast, they walk into surprises."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: A company only needs a budget, not a forecast.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "Good financial management needs both" — usar só um não basta.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James falando com a nova líder de departamento. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome to the team. Let me explain two words you will hear a lot here: budget and forecast.

Your budget is your plan. We set it before the year starts. It says how much you can spend each month. You agreed to it, so you must stay inside it. That is the discipline part. Please do not spend more than your budget.

But things change during the year. Maybe a project costs more. Maybe you earn less than we hoped. So every month, I want you to send me a forecast. A forecast is just an updated guess. It tells me where you are really going, not where we planned to go.

Why do we need both? The budget keeps you accountable. The forecast keeps the picture honest. If you only use the budget, you will walk into surprises. If you only use the forecast, you will spend with no limit.

So here is the simple rule. Live inside your budget. Update your forecast every month. Talk to me early if the two numbers start to move apart. That gap tells us a lot.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is a budget, according to James?
items.why: "Your budget is your plan. We set it before the year starts."

items.q: How often does James want a forecast?
options: Only when there is a problem
items.why: "every month, I want you to send me a forecast."

items.q: What should the new lead do if the two numbers start to move apart?
items.why: "Talk to me early if the two numbers start to move apart."

items.q: James suggests that using only a budget will make the team…
items.why: Inferência: "If you only use the budget, you will walk into surprises."

items.q: How would you best describe James's tone?
items.why: Inferência: ele dá as boas-vindas e explica com regras simples — é acolhedor e didático.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We made a budget for the whole year." A budget is…
items.why: Budget = orçamento: o plano de quanto gastar e ganhar.

items.q: "Our forecast says sales will grow." A forecast is…
options: an updated guess about the future
a list of costs from last year
items.why: Forecast = previsão: um palpite atualizado sobre o futuro.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We must not ___ more money than the plan allows."
items.why: To spend = gastar dinheiro.

items.q: "Each team is accountable for its numbers." Accountable means…
items.why: Accountable = responsável: quem responde pelo resultado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A good forecast keeps the picture ___, showing the real situation."
items.why: Honest = honesto: mostra a realidade, sem esconder.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre dinheiro. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new budget next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = colocar em prática, começar a usar.

items.q: "Let's keep an eye on the numbers this month." This means to…
items.why: Keep an eye on = ficar de olho, observar com atenção.

items.q: "We are trying to cut costs this year." To cut costs means to…
items.why: Cut costs = cortar custos, reduzir gastos.

items.q: "The team is over budget again." This means they…
items.why: Over budget = acima do orçamento, gastou mais do que o planejado.
